::: {.callout-important}
## Synthetic data

This project contains synthetic data and analysis created for demonstration
purposes only. Aurora Lending Group is a fictional company.
:::

Run this file one cell at a time in Positron on Amazon SageMaker. Use
Ctrl+Enter, or Cmd+Enter on a Mac. You can also render the whole file with
`uv run quarto render analysis/walkthrough_finance.qmd`.

Each section is one step of the demo.

## 1. No keys and no setup

The Positron image holds an AWS profile that asks the Studio app for
credentials. `boto3` therefore finds the SageMaker execution role by itself.

```{python}
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import boto3
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

# Find the repository root, so this file works from any directory.
here = Path.cwd()
repo = next((p for p in [here, *here.parents] if (p / "config.py").exists()), here)
sys.path.insert(0, str(repo))

import athena
import config

session = boto3.Session(region_name=config.REGION)
identity = session.client("sts").get_caller_identity()
arn = identity["Arn"]
print(f"account {identity['Account']}")
print(f"role    {arn.split('/')[-2] if '/' in arn else arn}")
print(f"region  {config.REGION}")
```

## 2. The governed catalog

AWS Glue is the catalog. Athena is the engine. Nothing was copied here.

```{python}
athena.tables("aurora_lending")
```

## 3. A query, straight into a DataFrame

The workgroup `primary` has no default output location. Every query must
therefore pass a staging location, or Athena returns an error.

```{python}
loans = athena.query(
    """
    SELECT f.loan_id,
           f.origination_date,
           f.fico_at_origination,
           f.dti,
           f.apr,
           f.term_months,
           CAST(f.principal_amount AS double)    AS principal_amount,
           CAST(f.outstanding_balance AS double) AS outstanding_balance,
           f.employment_length_years,
           f.purpose,
           f.charged_off,
           b.state,
           b.income_band,
           b.homeownership,
           p.product_name
    FROM fct_loan_performance f
    JOIN dim_borrower b     ON b.borrower_id = f.borrower_id
    JOIN dim_loan_product p ON p.product_id  = f.product_id
    """,
    "aurora_lending",
)
print(f"{len(loans):,} loans and {len(loans.columns)} columns")
loans.head()
```

## 4. Open this in the Data Explorer

Click `loans` in the Variables pane. The Data Explorer then sorts any column,
filters rows, and shows a summary of every column, with no code. Take your time
on this step.

```{python}
loans.describe()
```

## 5. Where is the risk?

```{python}
loans["fico_band"] = pd.cut(
    loans["fico_at_origination"],
    bins=[579, 620, 660, 700, 740, 780, 850],
    labels=["580-619", "620-659", "660-699", "700-739", "740-779", "780+"],
)
loans["vintage"] = pd.to_datetime(loans["origination_date"]).dt.year

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4))

by_band = loans.groupby("fico_band", observed=True)["charged_off"].mean() * 100
by_band.plot.bar(ax=ax1, color="#447099", rot=0, width=0.72)
ax1.set(title="Charge-off rate by FICO band", xlabel="FICO at origination",
        ylabel="charge-off rate (%)")

by_vintage = loans.pivot_table(index="vintage", columns="fico_band",
                               values="charged_off", observed=True) * 100
by_vintage.plot(ax=ax2, marker="o", linewidth=1.6, colormap="viridis")
ax2.set(title="Charge-off rate by year", xlabel="year of origination", ylabel="")
ax2.legend(title="FICO band", fontsize=7, ncol=2, frameon=False)

for ax in (ax1, ax2):
    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.25)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Credit quality is the strongest driver. The newest years have less time on
book, so their rates are still rising.

## 6. Where is the money?

A rate alone does not size the problem. This chart puts the balance at risk
next to the rate.

```{python}
by_purpose = (
    loans.groupby("purpose")
    .agg(rate=("charged_off", "mean"),
         exposure=("outstanding_balance", "sum"))
    .sort_values("rate")
)
by_purpose["rate"] *= 100
by_purpose["exposure"] /= 1e6

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4))
labels = [p.replace("_", " ") for p in by_purpose.index]
bars = ax.barh(labels, by_purpose["rate"], color="#447099")
ax.set(title="Charge-off rate and balance outstanding, by loan purpose",
       xlabel="charge-off rate (%)", ylabel="")
for bar, money in zip(bars, by_purpose["exposure"]):
    ax.text(bar.get_width() + 0.15, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height() / 2,
            f"${money:,.0f}M outstanding", va="center", fontsize=8, color="#404041")
ax.set_xlim(0, by_purpose["rate"].max() * 1.55)
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
ax.grid(axis="x", alpha=0.25)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## 7. Score the book with the hosted model

SageMaker hosts the model on a real-time endpoint. This cell sends an HTTPS
request, which the same execution role authorizes. Nothing loads locally.

```{python}
FEATURES = ["fico_at_origination", "dti", "apr", "term_months",
            "principal_amount", "employment_length_years", "purpose"]

sample = loans.sample(1_000, random_state=20260821).copy()
runtime = session.client("sagemaker-runtime")
scored = True

try:
    response = runtime.invoke_endpoint(
        EndpointName=config.FINANCE.endpoint,
        ContentType="application/json",
        Body=json.dumps({"instances": sample[FEATURES].to_dict(orient="records")}),
    )
    sample["risk_score"] = json.loads(response["Body"].read())["predictions"]
    print(f"scored {len(sample):,} loans on {config.FINANCE.endpoint}")
except Exception as err:  # noqa: BLE001
    # The endpoint exists only around the time of a session. Report what to do,
    # and let the rest of the file still run.
    scored = False
    print(f"The endpoint {config.FINANCE.endpoint} did not answer.")
    print(f"  {type(err).__name__}")
    print("  Deploy it:  uv run python ml/train_and_deploy.py --domain finance")
```

```{python}
if scored:
    display(sample[["loan_id", "fico_at_origination", "dti", "purpose",
                    "risk_score", "charged_off"]].head(10))
```

## 8. Does the model rank the risk?

Sort by predicted risk, cut into ten equal groups, then compare the prediction
against the charge-off rate that each group reached.

```{python}
if scored:
    sample["decile"] = pd.qcut(sample["risk_score"], 10, labels=False,
                               duplicates="drop") + 1
    lift = sample.groupby("decile").agg(
        loans=("loan_id", "size"),
        mean_predicted=("risk_score", "mean"),
        actual_chargeoff=("charged_off", "mean"),
        exposure=("outstanding_balance", "sum"),
    )
    lift[["mean_predicted", "actual_chargeoff"]] *= 100
    display(lift.round(2))
```

```{python}
if scored:
    fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4))

    width = 0.38
    x = np.arange(len(lift))
    ax1.bar(x - width / 2, lift["mean_predicted"], width,
            label="predicted", color="#447099")
    ax1.bar(x + width / 2, lift["actual_chargeoff"], width,
            label="actual", color="#ee6331")
    ax1.set(title="Predicted rate against actual rate, by decile",
            xlabel="risk decile, 10 is the riskiest", ylabel="charge-off rate (%)")
    ax1.set_xticks(x, lift.index)
    ax1.legend(frameon=False)

    # A model that ranks well puts most of the losses in the top deciles.
    ordered = lift.sort_index(ascending=False)
    captured = (ordered["actual_chargeoff"] * ordered["loans"]).cumsum()
    captured = captured / captured.iloc[-1] * 100
    share = np.arange(1, len(ordered) + 1) / len(ordered) * 100
    ax2.plot(share, captured.to_numpy(), marker="o", color="#9a4665")
    ax2.plot([0, 100], [0, 100], linestyle="--", color="#a0a0a0",
             label="no model")
    ax2.set(title="Share of all charge-offs captured",
            xlabel="share of the book reviewed (%)",
            ylabel="share of charge-offs found (%)")
    ax2.legend(frameon=False)

    for ax in (ax1, ax2):
        ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
        ax.grid(alpha=0.25)
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
```

```{python}
# | output: asis
if scored:
    base = sample["charged_off"].mean() * 100
    top = lift.loc[10, "actual_chargeoff"]
    two = (sample.loc[sample["decile"] >= 9, "charged_off"].sum()
           / max(sample["charged_off"].sum(), 1) * 100)
    print(f"The base rate for this sample is **{base:.1f}%**. "
          f"The riskiest decile reaches **{top:.1f}%**, which is "
          f"**{top / base:.1f}** times the base rate. "
          f"The top two deciles hold **{two:.0f}%** of all charge-offs.")
```

## 9. The experiment history

Every model that trained for this demo is a run on the SageMaker managed MLflow
tracking server. Each run holds the parameters, the metrics, and the scorecard
that the run produced.

```{python}
from ml.tracking import Tracker

tracker = Tracker.connect(quiet=True)
runs = None if tracker is None else tracker.runs(config.FINANCE)

if tracker is None:
    print("The MLflow tracking server is not running.")
    print("Start it:  uv run python ml/mlflow_server.py start")
elif runs is None or len(runs) == 0:
    print("The server is running, but this experiment has no runs.")
    print("Train first:  uv run python ml/train_and_deploy.py --domain finance")
else:
    print(f"{len(runs)} runs in the experiment `aurora-lending-charge-off`")
    display(runs)
```

```{python}
if runs is not None and len(runs) > 0:
    best = runs.sort_values("test_auc", ascending=False)
    colors = ["#447099" if flag == "true" else "#a8bcd0"
              for flag in best.get("deployed", ["false"] * len(best))]

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 3.6))
    ax.barh(best["runName"], best["test_auc"], color=colors)
    ax.set(title="Test AUC by feature set. The dark bar is the model on the endpoint.",
           xlabel="test AUC", ylabel="",
           xlim=(0, max(1.0, best["test_auc"].max() * 1.15)))
    for y, value in enumerate(best["test_auc"]):
        ax.text(value + 0.01, y, f"{value:.3f}", va="center", fontsize=9)
    ax.invert_yaxis()
    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
    ax.grid(axis="x", alpha=0.25)
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
```

Credit quality alone gets most of the way. The purpose of the loan, its size,
and its term add the rest. The tracking server records that comparison, so the
next person to open this work can see which features earned their place.

Open the MLflow UI to compare the runs, read the parameters, and download the
scorecard that each run produced.

```{python}
if tracker is not None:
    url = tracker.ui_url()
    print(url if url else "No signed URL. Is the server running?")
```
